q: 1. Where is the permanent headquarters (Secretariat) of SAARC located?
explain: The permanent Secretariat was established in Kathmandu on January 16, 1987. Dhaka is where the founding summit took place; Islamabad and New Delhi host major summits and specialized bodies.

q: 2. Who inaugurated the SAARC Secretariat in Kathmandu on January 16, 1987?
explain: King Birendra officially inaugurated the permanent Secretariat in Kathmandu on January 16, 1987. Ziaur Rahman died prior to the inauguration; Abul Ahsan was the first Secretary-General inaugurated; King Gyanendra represented Nepal in 2005.

q: 3. What is the official motto of SAARC?
options: Deeper Integration for Peace and Prosperity
explain: This is the official motto of SAARC, emphasizing economic harmonization and peace. The other options represent generic regional cooperation phrases not officially adopted by the Charter.

q: 4. Which is the latest SAARC country with whom Nepal has established formal diplomatic relation?
explain: Bhutan is the most recent SAARC nation with which Nepal established formal diplomatic ties (June 1983).

q: 5. When did the concept of regional cooperation in South Asia first get raised by President Ziaur Rahman?
explain: President Ziaur Rahman first raised the concept on May 2, 1980. December 8, 1985 is the actual establishment date; April 11, 1993 is when SAPTA was signed; January 1, 2006 is when SAFTA entered into force.

q: 6. Where did the Foreign Ministers meet in August 1983 to launch the Integrated Programme of Action (IPA)?
explain: The Foreign Ministers met in New Delhi in August 1983, formally launching the Integrated Programme of Action (IPA) under SARC. Bangalore, Male, and Islamabad hosted subsequent summits.

q: 7. When was Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) established?
explain: APEC was established in 1989. Its headquarters is in Singapore, and its first meeting was held in Australia in 1989.

q: 8. How many observer countries are currently associated with SAARC?
explain: SAARC currently has nine official observer nations (Australia, China, EU, Iran, Japan, South Korea, Mauritius, Myanmar, and USA). Seven represents the founding countries; Eight represents the current member states.

q: 9. Which country formally joined as the eighth member state of SAARC on April 4, 2007?
explain: Afghanistan became the eighth member on April 4, 2007 at the 14th Summit in New Delhi. Maldives, Bhutan, and Sri Lanka are founding member states established in 1985.

q: 10. Which of the following represents the correct count of landlocked countries in SAARC?
explain: There are three landlocked member countries in SAARC: Nepal, Bhutan, and Afghanistan. Two refers to island countries (Sri Lanka and Maldives).

q: 11. Which is the smallest SAARC country by area and population?
explain: Maldives is the smallest country by area (298 sq km) and population rank (8th). Bhutan is 7th in both area and population ranks.

q: 12. What is the geographical area of the Maldives as recorded in the SAARC country profiles?
explain: The country profile confirms Maldives' territory spans 298 sq km. 3.287 million sq km is India's area.

q: 13. Which SAARC nation has 'Shora' as the official name of its parliament?
explain: Afghanistan's parliament is known as 'Shora'. Bangladesh's is Jatiya Sangsad, Bhutan's is Tshogdu, and Maldives' is Majlis.

q: 14. What is the time difference of Bangladesh and Bhutan with Nepal?
explain: Bangladesh and Bhutan are both +15 minutes ahead of Nepal standard time. -0:15 is India and Sri Lanka; -0:45 is Pakistan and Maldives.

q: 15. Which SAARC country is at -0:15 minutes behind Nepal's local time?
explain: India and Sri Lanka are both -15 minutes behind Nepal time. Afghanistan is -1:15 behind; Pakistan and Maldives are -0:45 behind Nepal.

q: 16. How many Articles are there in the official SAARC Charter?
explain: The SAARC Charter comprises exactly ten Articles and a Preamble. Seven is the number of founding nations; Eight is the number of current members.

q: 17. Which of the following is NOT one of the three principles laid down in Article II of the SAARC Charter?
options: Cooperation shall complement bilateral and multilateral frameworks
Decisions shall be taken on the basis of a simple majority
Cooperation shall not be inconsistent with bilateral and multilateral obligations
explain: Article II contains no voting provisions. Decisions under SAARC are made on the basis of consensus (unanimity), not majority. The other options are the actual principles defined in Article II.

q: 18. How many core principles of cooperation are defined under Article II of the SAARC Charter?
explain: Article II contains exactly three core operational principles. Five refers to specialized bodies; Ten refers to Articles.

q: 19. Which of the following is a primary objective of SAARC under Article I?
options: To establish a common military defense pact
To promote the welfare of the peoples of South Asia and improve their quality of life
To enforce a single currency across South Asia
To merge the administrative ministries of member states
explain: This is the first and primary objective under Article I. The other options are military/currency items not in the Charter.

q: 20. Which country's representative was the first Secretary-General of SAARC?
explain: The first SG, Abul Ahsan, represented Bangladesh. India, Pakistan, and Nepal contributed Secretaries-General at a later stage.

q: 21. What is the tenure of the SAARC Secretary-General as decided at the Ninth Summit?
explain: The Ninth Summit extended the SG's tenure from two to three years. The other options are incorrect based on current rules.

q: 22. Who is the first and only female Secretary-General of SAARC to date?
explain: She was the first and only female SG in SAARC history. Benazir Bhutto was a Summit delegate, Sushila Karki was Nepal's chief justice, and Annalena Baerbock is Germany's minister.

q: 23. In which year did Fathimath Dhiyana Saeed resign from her post of Secretary-General?
explain: She resigned in March 2012 before completing her term due to domestic political alignments. The other options represent other years.

q: 24. Who succeeded Fathimath Dhiyana Saeed as Secretary-General on March 12, 2012?
explain: Ahmed Saleem (Maldives) succeeded her to serve the remaining term. The other options are other Secretaries-General.

q: 25. Which SAARC summits were held in Kathmandu, Nepal?
explain: Kathmandu hosted these four summits in 1987, 2002, 2014, and 2023. The other options list summits hosted elsewhere.

q: 26. Where was the 19th SAARC Summit scheduled to be held before its cancellation?
explain: The 19th Summit was scheduled to be held in Islamabad. The other options represent other locations.

q: 27. Which country has hosted SAARC summits exactly three times, similar to Nepal?
explain: These nations, along with Nepal, have hosted summits exactly three times (or four for Nepal now). The other options are incorrect groupings.

q: 28. Which SAARC Summit was held in Kathmandu, Nepal, in the year 2023?
explain: The 21st Summit was convened in Kathmandu, Nepal, in 2023. The 18th Summit was in 2014; the 19th and 20th were scheduled or postponed.

q: 29. Who represented Nepal at the 8th SAARC Summit in New Delhi (1995)?
explain: PM Manmohan Adhikari represented Nepal at the 8th Summit in New Delhi (1995). The other options represented Nepal at other summits.

q: 30. How many summits did King Birendra Bir Bikram Shah attend as Nepal's representative?
explain: King Birendra represented Nepal at the 1st, 2nd, 3rd, and 4th Summits. The other options do not match his record.

q: 31. When did the SAARC Agreement on Trade in Services (SATIS) officially enter into force?
explain: SATIS entered into force on November 29, 2012. April 2010 is the signing year; January 1, 2006 is SAFTA's active date.

q: 32. Where is the headquarters of the SAARC Development Fund (SDF) situated?
explain: The SAARC Development Fund is headquartered in Thimphu. The other options host other specialized bodies or centers.

q: 33. In which country is the South Asian University (SAU) located?
explain: The South Asian University (SAU) is an international university located in New Delhi, India. The other options are other member nations.

q: 34. The SAARC Poverty Alleviation program was implemented in which district of Nepal?
explain: The SAARC Poverty Alleviation program was implemented in Nepal's Makwanpur district. The other options are other districts of Nepal not associated with this program.

q: 35. When and under which treaty was SAARC officially established?
explain: SAARC was formally established on 8 December 1985 through the Dhaka Declaration, signed at the first SAARC Summit.

q: 36. Which of the following given dignitaries is/are not the signatories on the Charter of SAARC?
explain: Ziaur Rahman of Bangladesh, who first proposed the idea of regional cooperation, died in 1981, before the SAARC Charter was signed in 1985, so he could not be a signatory.

q: 37. Which one of the following is not an objective of the SAARC charter?
options: To promote the welfare of the peoples of South Asia
To accelerate economic growth in South Asia
To contribute to mutual trust in South Asia
explain: "Maintaining international peace" is a UN Charter objective, not a stated objective of the SAARC Charter, which focuses on regional welfare, growth, and cooperation.

q: 38. For which of following, the SAARC movement was launched?
explain: SAARC was launched with the core aim of promoting regional cooperation among South Asian nations.

q: 39. How many articles are there in Charter of SAARC?
explain: The SAARC Charter, signed in 1985, contains 10 Articles covering objectives, principles, institutional structure, and administration.

q: 40. How many Apex bodies are there in SAARC?
explain: SAARC has 6 recognized Apex bodies representing professional and civil society groups across the region.

q: 41. Which is the executive body of SAARC?
explain: The Standing Committee, composed of Foreign Secretaries, functions as the executive body overseeing programme implementation.

q: 42. Who are the members of Council of Ministers of SAARC?
options: Ministers of foreign affairs of the members state
Ministers of prime ministers of the members state
Ministers of defence ministers of the members state
Ministers of home ministers of the members state
explain: The SAARC Council of Ministers comprises the Foreign Ministers of member states and meets to formulate policy.

q: 43. Who is the Nepali artist to design the SAARC emblem?
explain: The SAARC emblem was designed by Nepali artist Shailendra Kumar Mahrajan.

q: 44. When was SAFTA (South Asian Free Trade Agreement) signed during 12th Summit in Islamabad on?
explain: SAFTA was signed on 6 January 2004 at the 12th SAARC Summit in Islamabad.

q: 45. Which of the following is\are not the observer of South Asian Association for Regional Co-operation (SAARC)?
explain: SAARC observers include Japan, USA, South Korea, China, EU and others, but the UK is not among SAARC's observer states.

q: 46. Who is Current Secretary General of South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation (SAARC)?
explain: As per this reference material, Golam Sarwar is listed as the current Secretary-General of SAARC.

q: 47. Considering the area of the SAARC nations, which of the following is the right order of those Nations, from the smallest to the largest?
options: Maldives, Bhutan, Nepal, Sri Lanka, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Afghanistan, India
Bhutan, Maldives, Nepal, Sri Lanka, Bangladesh, Afghanistan, Pakistan, India
Maldives, Bhutan, Sri Lanka, Nepal, Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Pakistan, India
Maldives, Bhutan, Sri Lanka, Nepal, Bangladesh, Afghanistan, Pakistan, India
explain: By land area, the correct ascending order of SAARC nations is Maldives, Bhutan, Sri Lanka, Nepal, Bangladesh, Afghanistan, Pakistan, India.

q: 48. Which is the first SAARC country to provide e-passport to its citizens?
explain: The Maldives was the first SAARC country to introduce e-passports for its citizens.

q: 49. How many land-locked countries are there in South Asian Association for Regional Co-Operation (SAARC)?
explain: SAARC has 3 land-locked countries: Nepal, Bhutan, and Afghanistan.

q: 50. How many water-locked countries are there in South Asian Association for Regional Co Operation (SAARC)?
explain: SAARC has 2 water-locked (island) countries: Sri Lanka and Maldives.

q: 51. What is the Currency of Bhutan called?
explain: Bhutan's official currency is the Ngultrum, which is pegged to the Indian Rupee.

q: 52. How many times that the SAARC summits held in Nepal?
explain: Nepal has hosted SAARC Summits three times: the 3rd (1987), 11th (2002), and 18th (2014) Summits, all held in Kathmandu.

q: 53. What percentage of total expenditure of SAARC secretariat is bear by Nepal?
explain: As per this reference, Nepal bears 10.72% of the total expenditure of the SAARC Secretariat, based on the organization's cost-sharing formula.

q: 54. BIMSTEC permanent Headquarter at Dhaka was established on --------
explain: The BIMSTEC Permanent Secretariat in Dhaka was formally established on 13 September 2014.

q: 55. Where was the 4th BIMSTEC summit held in 2018 A.D.?
explain: The 4th BIMSTEC Summit was held in Kathmandu, Nepal in August 2018.

q: 56. Currently, which country is the chair of BIMSTEC?
explain: As per this reference material, Bangladesh currently holds the chairmanship of BIMSTEC.

q: 57. How many sectoral area of cooperation are indentified by the fifth BIMSTEC Summit held in Columbo, Sri Lanka?
explain: The 5th BIMSTEC Summit, held in Colombo, Sri Lanka, streamlined cooperation into 7 broad sectoral areas.

q: 58. Which Prime Minister of Nepal attended the 6th BIMSTEC Summit?
explain: K.P. Sharma Oli represented Nepal as Prime Minister at the 6th BIMSTEC Summit.

q: 59. What is the theme of 6th Bay of Bengal Initiative for Multi-Sectoral Technical and Economic Cooperation (BIMSTEC) Summit?
options: Towards a Peaceful, Prosperous & Sustainable Bay of Bengal Region
Prosperous Economies, Healthy Peoples & Sustainable Bay of Bengal Region
explain: The 6th BIMSTEC Summit in Bangkok (2025) was held under the theme 'Prosperous, Resilient, and Open BIMSTEC'.

q: 60. Which sector of BIMSTEC is leading by Nepal?
explain: Nepal is designated as the lead country for the People-to-People Contact sector within BIMSTEC's sectoral cooperation framework.
